question: In the precomputed SCAPS sweep of absorber thickness, what is the simulated PCE at 200 nm and at 1000 nm, and how does PCE change with thickness?
final_answer:
Based on the precomputed SCAPS thickness sweep (`perovskite_nip.def`):

- **Simulated PCE at 200 nm:** **24.29%** ($V_{oc} = 1.400\text{ V}$, $J_{sc} = 19.14\text{ mA/cm}^2$, $\text{FF} = 90.62\%$)
- **Simulated PCE at 1000 nm:** **32.14%** ($V_{oc} = 1.365\text{ V}$, $J_{sc} = 26.06\text{ mA/cm}^2$, $\text{FF} = 90.40\%$)

**How PCE changes with thickness:**
PCE increases monotonically across the swept range from 200 nm to 1000 nm (overall positive trend, relative increase of ~32.33%). This gain is driven primarily by increased optical absorption and photogenerated carrier collection leading to higher short-circuit current density ($J_{sc}$ rises from $19.14$ to $26.06\text{ mA/cm}^2$), which outweighs the slight decreases observed in open-circuit voltage ($V_{oc}$ drops from $1.400\text{ V}$ to $1.365\text{ V}$) and fill factor ($\text{FF}$ drops slightly from $90.62\%$ to $90.40\%$).
